section: 73rd Amendment - Part IX, Eleventh Schedule, three-tier structure, Gram Sabha, reservations, State Election Commission

accepted.s: In 2026, how many village panchayats of Andhra Pradesh won the National Panchayat Awards?
accepted.x: Five village panchayats of Andhra Pradesh won the National Panchayat Awards in 2026.
accepted.tq: Use the exact numerical figure rather than inferring from the number of tiers or districts.

accepted.s: The Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Department received a national award in 2026 for the:
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Department won a national award for the second year running.
accepted.tq: Pay attention to time expressions such as ‘second year running’.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is identified as a reason for the uneven devolution of funds, functions and functionaries to Panchayats?
o: The 29 subjects are voluntary for devolution
The State Election Commission controls all Panchayat finances
Panchayats are excluded from the Constitution
The Eleventh Schedule contains no subjects
accepted.x: Devolution remains uneven because the 29 subjects listed for Panchayats are voluntary in implementation.
accepted.tq: Link the governance problem to the stated institutional cause rather than to election machinery.

accepted.s: The recent women-leadership drives in Panchayati Raj institutions seek to move beyond numerical reservation towards:
o: Replacement of elected bodies by officials
Exclusive representation of women in all tiers
accepted.x: The stated objective is to convert numerical reservation into real empowerment of women leaders.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise policy objective behind a reform initiative.

accepted.s:
With reference to Andhra Pradesh Panchayati Raj, consider the following statements:
1. The Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act was enacted in 1994.
2. The Act is Act No. 13 of 1994.
3. PESA is relevant to agency areas of Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act is the 1994 Act No. 13, and PESA applies to the State’s agency areas.
accepted.tq: Check each statement independently before selecting the inclusive combination.

accepted.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the Mandal Parishad is also referred to as the:
accepted.x: The intermediate tier is called the Mandal Parishad, also known as the Mandal Praja Parishad.
accepted.tq: Test the official equivalent name of the intermediate Panchayat tier.

accepted.s: The 2026 local body elections in Andhra Pradesh are being conducted under the State Election Commission headed by:
accepted.x: The 2026 local body polls in Andhra Pradesh are stated to be under SEC Punetha.
accepted.tq: Match the election process with the authority named in the current-affairs fact.

accepted.s: The 74th Constitutional Amendment is associated with which of the following combinations?
o: Part X, Articles 244–244A and Fifth Schedule with 29 subjects
Part IXB, Articles 243ZH–243ZT and Ninth Schedule with 18 subjects
Part IX, Articles 243A–243O and Eleventh Schedule with 29 subjects
Part IXA, Articles 243P–243ZG and Twelfth Schedule with 18 subjects
accepted.x: The 74th Amendment inserted Part IXA, comprising Articles 243P to 243ZG, and the Twelfth Schedule containing 18 subjects.
accepted.tq: Use the Part–Article range–Schedule combination to identify the correct constitutional amendment.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about SabhaSaar is correct?
o: It is the first AI tool for preparing Gram Sabha minutes and was piloted in Tripura on Bhashini.
It is an urban governance tool piloted in Andhra Pradesh for municipal budgets.
It is a State Election Commission portal used only for voter registration.
It is a Finance Commission application used for distributing grants to Zilla Parishads.
accepted.x: SabhaSaar is described as the first AI tool for Gram Sabha minutes; it was piloted in Tripura on the Bhashini platform.
accepted.tq: Identify the tool by its function, pilot location and platform together.

accepted.s: By November 2025, SabhaSaar had been used by approximately how many Gram Panchayats for how many Gram Sabhas?
o: 1.38 lakh Gram Panchayats for 1 lakh Gram Sabhas
1 lakh Gram Panchayats for 1.38 lakh Gram Sabhas
accepted.x: By November 2025, approximately one lakh Gram Panchayats had used SabhaSaar for 1.38 lakh Gram Sabhas.
accepted.tq: Read paired figures carefully and do not reverse the users and the meetings covered.

accepted.s: The 30 years of which legislation or framework were marked in the context of recent Panchayati Raj developments?
o: The Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994
The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996
accepted.x: Thirty years of PESA—the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) framework—were marked.
accepted.tq: Distinguish PESA from the constitutional amendment and the State Panchayat Act.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the approximate institutional spread of Panchayats in Andhra Pradesh mentioned in the context of 2026?
o: About 1.38 lakh Gram Panchayats and 29 Zilla Parishads
About 15,000 or more Gram Panchayats and 13 Zilla Parishads
About 5,000 Gram Panchayats and 8 Zilla Parishads
About 1,000 Gram Panchayats and 3 Zilla Parishads
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh has about 15,000 or more Gram Panchayats and 13 Zilla Parishads as stated in the current context.
accepted.tq: Keep approximate figures and institutional levels aligned instead of borrowing figures from another programme.

accepted.s: Which State was the first to launch Panchayati Raj Institutions, and when did Andhra Pradesh launch them?
o: Andhra Pradesh first on 1 November 1959; Rajasthan second on 2 October 1959
Rajasthan first on 2 October 1959; Andhra Pradesh second on 1 November 1959
Rajasthan first on 1 November 1959; Andhra Pradesh second on 2 October 1959
Andhra Pradesh first on 2 October 1959; Rajasthan second on 1 November 1959
accepted.x: Rajasthan was the first State to launch PRIs on 2 October 1959, while Andhra Pradesh was the second on 1 November 1959.
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence with the first and second States and verify both dates.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 2026 urban local body elections in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Elections are proposed for 100 of the 123 urban local bodies.
2. Articles 243-U, 243-K and 243-ZA are relevant to the process.
3. The elections concern only Gram Panchayats.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the process concerns urban local bodies, not only Gram Panchayats.
accepted.tq: Reject the statement that changes the rural–urban scope of the election.

accepted.s: A proposal to postpone local body elections in Andhra Pradesh was linked to the demand that the elections should await the:
o: Constitution of a new Finance Commission
Delimitation of all Lok Sabha constituencies
Completion of the SIR of electoral rolls
Publication of the next Census alone
accepted.x: The demand to postpone the polls was linked to completion of the SIR of electoral rolls.
accepted.tq: Match the proposed electoral action with the specific procedural reason given for it.

accepted.s: The issue concerning the 34 per cent BC reservation in Andhra Pradesh local bodies is that the BC quota together with SC/ST shares must remain within the:
o: Fifty per cent ceiling associated with the Gawali principle
accepted.x: The 34 per cent BC quota, together with SC/ST reservations, is required to pass the 50 per cent ceiling associated with Gawali’s ruling or principle.
accepted.tq: Add the reservation components conceptually and identify the applicable ceiling.

accepted.s: Which of the following initiatives is intended to counter token representation of women in Panchayati Raj institutions?
o: Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan and Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats
PESA and the Sixteenth Finance Commission grants
accepted.x: The Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan and Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats are intended to promote substantive women’s leadership and counter token representation.
accepted.tq: Match the initiative with its stated social-governance objective.

accepted.s: Under the Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayat initiative, how many such Panchayats are envisaged per district?
accepted.x: The initiative envisages one Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayat per district.
accepted.tq: Test the exact unit of implementation rather than the total number of districts.

accepted.s: Which of the following is regarded as one of the clearest achievements of the 73rd and 74th Amendments in the stated assessment?
o: Complete uniformity in the devolution of all 29 subjects
Abolition of State Election Commissions and increased official appointments
Regular elections and near-50 per cent representation of women
Replacement of Gram Sabhas by urban local bodies
accepted.x: Regular elections and near-50 per cent representation of women are identified as the clearest achievements of the Amendments.
accepted.tq: Distinguish recognised achievements from unresolved criticism about devolution.

accepted.s: OWMS in Andhra Pradesh is being used for online monitoring of:
o: 800 or more water and sewerage projects in 123 urban local bodies
accepted.x: The Online Water Monitoring System is used to monitor more than 800 water and sewerage projects across 123 urban local bodies.
accepted.tq: Link the monitoring system to its sector and preserve both scale figures.

accepted.s: Which institution of Andhra Pradesh was ranked first nationally in the context of the 2026 Panchayati Raj awards?
o: The Chittoor District Panchayat Raj Centre
The Mandal Praja Parishad of Chittoor
The Andhra Pradesh Urban Water Monitoring Society
accepted.x: The Chittoor District Panchayat Raj Centre, or Chittoor DPRC, was ranked first nationally.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the award-winning district resource institution from the State-level department and election body.
